title: Shopify Subscription Phone Support: A Decision Guide for Cancellation and Failed-Payment Calls
summary: A Shopify subscription phone-support guide covering voice AI for cancellation and failed-payment calls, human escalation, and pilot testing.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- Voice AI can answer policy questions without account access. After caller verification, it can explain a subscription status or failed payment only when it can read current, authoritative records.[Recharge separates read permissions from write permissions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/2021-11/subscriptions) , so a successful lookup does not authorize a cancellation.
- A voice agent can present a brand-approved retention offer to an eligible caller. Any plan change needs explicit acceptance, a record of that acceptance, and separately tested authorization to make the change. If the caller declines and still wants to cancel, the agent must not delay the request.
- Route disputes, refund requests, payment-method changes, uncertain account matches, and unavailable records to a person. Treat cancellation execution as a human task until your pilot proves the full authorization and confirmation path.
- Before expanding call volume, test whether the stated outcome matches the account record and whether a receiving agent gets enough context to finish an escalated call.


## Why this call type needs its own decision framework


Cancellation and failed-payment calls require decisions about money, customer consent, and account state in the same conversation. A caller asking why a charge failed may need a factual status answer. A caller disputing that charge needs an investigation, and a caller who accepts an offer may be authorizing a change to future billing. Those requests should not follow the same automation rule.


If you lead support at a high-call-volume Shopify subscription brand using Recharge and Gorgias, decide what your voice agent may say, what it may change, and when a person must take over before you run a pilot. A matched phone number may help locate an account, but it does not establish that the caller can authorize a cancellation. Your pilot also needs to check the live phone route. An escalation rule cannot protect a caller if the transfer reaches an unanswered line.


This decision guide addresses those call boundaries rather than ranking vendors or prescribing integration steps. Use the[Shopify platform comparison](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/best-voice-ai-shopify-phone-support) for vendor selection and the[Shopify–Recharge–Gorgias workflow guide](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/voice-ai-shopify-recharge-gorgias-phone-support) for implementation details.


## The call-flow decision table


For a Shopify subscription line, use this table as a proposed pilot boundary, not a list of enabled integrations. Recharge documents separate[read_subscriptions and write_subscriptions permissions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/2021-11/subscriptions) , with cancellation requiring a distinct action. Shopify’s[subscription-contract reference](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/customer/latest/objects/SubscriptionContract) describes a separate data model; access to it does not establish access to a retailer’s Recharge records. Neither permission establishes that SigmaMind AI can access or change a retailer’s Recharge subscriptions. You must identify the authoritative record and test the configured access before the agent gives an account-specific answer.


Call stage Voice AI may handle Route to a person when Proof needed in the pilot


Caller verification Explain general policy and run the retailer’s approved identity check before disclosing account details. The caller cannot verify, or the account match depends only on a phone number or email address. An unverified caller receives no subscription or payment details.


Caller changes their request Reassess the request when a status question becomes a cancellation, dispute, or payment-method request. The new request requires an action outside the approved read-only path. The agent stops the original flow and follows the boundary for the caller’s new request.


Subscription and status lookup After verification, report the specific subscription and status using authorized, current read access. Records conflict, the caller has multiple subscriptions that cannot be distinguished, or lookup fails. The spoken answer matches the correct authoritative record.


Cancellation request Capture the request for human handoff and explain the retailer’s cancellation policy. Send execution to a person by default. The caller wants cancellation completed, or the agent cannot establish which subscription they mean. The handoff preserves the requested subscription, the caller’s stated intent, and any deadline discussed. No agent-initiated cancellation occurs without separately proven write controls.


Retention offer Present a brand-approved offer only after an eligibility check. Ask for explicit acceptance before proposing any change. The caller declines, eligibility is unclear, or the caller asks to cancel without discussing offers. The tested consent log or handoff record distinguishes an accepted offer from a decline. A decline never blocks the cancellation request.


Failed-payment question After verification, explain a confirmed charge status or pending retry using authorized, current records. The status is missing or ambiguous, or the caller needs to change a payment method. The agent does not describe a pending retry as a successful payment and never requests a spoken card number.


Billing dispute Acknowledge the disputed charge and collect the details your retailer permits for handoff. The caller contests a charge, requests a refund, or reports suspected fraud. The agent makes no refund or liability promise, and the receiving person gets the disputed transaction details.


Permissions Use only the read access approved for the call. Treat cancellation and account changes as separate write actions. Access is denied, a write permission is absent, or the requested action exceeds the pilot’s approved scope. Tests confirm that denied access and lookup errors produce no disclosure or write.


Escalation Route eligible calls through the configured phone path. SigmaMind AI[documents warm and cold transfer options](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/transfer-call.md) . A required person is unavailable, or an earlier row requires human judgment. The receiving person confirms what context arrived. An unanswered transfer follows the retailer’s tested fallback.


## Read access versus write access, and why the line matters


Read access lets a voice agent report a subscription’s status without changing what the merchant will bill next.[Recharge’s API reference](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/2021-11/subscriptions) separates read_subscriptions from write_subscriptions and lists lookup separately from cancellation. A cancellation request therefore needs permission for a different action. Shopify’s[subscription-contract reference](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/customer/latest/objects/SubscriptionContract) describes Shopify subscription-contract data, which should not be assumed to match a retailer’s Recharge record. Neither set of permissions proves that a particular SigmaMind AI phone deployment can read or change a caller’s subscription.


Before the agent gives an account-specific answer, the caller must pass the merchant’s verification procedure. An incoming phone number or matched email can help locate an account, but neither proves ownership. The agent then needs a current record from the authoritative subscription source. If records conflict, a lookup fails, or the data may be stale, the agent should stop short of giving a definitive answer and transfer the call.


A subscription change needs a stricter chain of authorization. The merchant must enable the specific write action, define when the agent may use it, obtain the caller’s explicit consent, and log what the caller approved. After an authorized action, the agent should confirm the outcome only when a fresh read of the authoritative record shows the intended account state. Until a merchant has tested those steps and their failure cases, the agent should record cancellation intent and route execution to a person. A recorded request alone does not mean the subscription was canceled.


## Why voice transfer and ticket write-back are not the same thing


A voice transfer moves a call, but it does not create a Gorgias record.[SigmaMind AI’s transfer documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/transfer-call.md) describes cold and warm transfers, private whisper messages, and custom SIP headers. A whisper can give the receiving person context, while SIP headers can carry data if the receiving phone system accepts and uses them. Neither mechanism confirms that Gorgias received a ticket or call summary.


The[SigmaMind AI Gorgias integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/app-integration/gorgias.md) documents syncing macros, ticket tags, rules, and FAQs. It does not document automatic phone-call summary write-back. The[Gorgias marketplace listing for SigmaMind AI](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) describes ticket automation, but it does not establish that a phone transfer creates a ticket. If the retailer wants call summaries in Gorgias, it must establish a supported or custom path and test that the right record receives the right details. The[Shopify, Recharge, and Gorgias workflow guide](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/voice-ai-shopify-recharge-gorgias-phone-support) covers the implementation considerations.


In a pilot, check what the receiving agent hears and what Gorgias stores after the same call. Test an unanswered transfer too. If context fails to arrive or no person answers, the caller needs a defined fallback rather than an assurance that someone has the case.


## Retention offers: where consent becomes the control


A retention offer should enter a cancellation call only after the caller passes the retailer’s identity check and the agent confirms which subscription the caller wants to cancel. The retailer must define who qualifies for each offer. A discount or refund should never be presented as an automatic entitlement.


The agent can state an eligible offer and its terms, then ask whether the caller wants to accept it. An explicit spoken acceptance must be captured and logged before any plan change. Recharge[separates subscription reads from writes](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/2021-11/subscriptions) , so an agent’s ability to look up a plan does not establish permission to change it. Even with write access, you must prove that the caller authorized the specific change and that the resulting subscription state matches what the agent promised.


If the caller declines, the agent should continue the cancellation path without repeating the offer or treating silence as consent. Route the request to a person for execution unless your pilot has proven the retailer-authorized cancellation action, consent record, and independent confirmation of the final account state. Refunds, discounts, and offer eligibility follow retailer policy, not a voice platform default.


## Billing disputes and failed payments: what an agent can say versus must refer


A voice agent can explain a failed payment when it has verified the caller and retrieved a current, unambiguous charge record from the retailer’s authoritative source. For example, the agent can report that a charge failed and describe a pending retry if the available record confirms both facts. Recharge[documents charge lookup separately from refund and other charge actions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/2021-11/charges) . Its 90-day qualifier applies to included charge activities in a documented response, not to all charge history. If the record is missing, stale, or unclear, the agent should not guess at the cause or retry status.


A caller who says a charge was unauthorized, contests the amount, or requests a refund needs a person who can investigate and apply retailer policy. The agent can acknowledge the concern and transfer the call, but a successful lookup alone cannot settle a dispute. The receiving person should get the verified account and charge identifiers, the caller’s stated concern, and the facts the agent already checked, subject to the retailer’s data-sharing rules.


Payment details require a separate hard stop. The agent should not invite spoken card numbers or collect or correct a payment method in a recorded or transcribed call without a merchant-approved secure channel. The merchant must assess whether its own call recording, transcription, and payment flow meet its payment-card compliance requirements. If a caller starts reciting card details, the agent should interrupt and direct them to the approved channel.


## Designing the pilot: scenarios, failure handling, and handoff


Run the pilot through the phone number and routing you plan to use, with test accounts whose subscription and charge states you already know.[Batch simulations](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/playground/run-batch-simulations.md) can exercise scripted conversations, but you must test the live phone route and human handoff separately. Define the expected outcome for each case before placing the call.


Test call Passing behavior


Caller cannot verify identity The voice agent gives general policy information without disclosing account details or changing the subscription.


Account has multiple subscriptions The voice agent identifies which subscription the caller means before giving a billing answer. Ambiguity stops the account-specific answer.


Caller declines an offer and asks to cancel The voice agent captures the decision for handoff, stops presenting offers, and routes the cancellation for human execution unless you have separately proven an authorized cancellation workflow.


An authorized change receives an error or cannot be confirmed The voice agent does not claim the change succeeded. It preserves the request and error for a person to investigate, and the pilot checks the final authoritative record.


Failed charge has a pending retry The voice agent states the recorded charge and retry status without claiming that payment succeeded or promising when it will succeed.


Caller disputes a charge The voice agent transfers the caller for investigation rather than treating the dispute as a routine failed-payment question.


Part of the subscription lookup fails The voice agent withholds any answer that depends on the missing data and transfers the caller.


Lookup times out or hits a rate limit The voice agent explains that it cannot confirm the account state and does not guess or attempt a write.


Human line goes unanswered The call follows a tested fallback, such as another staffed queue or a merchant-approved callback process. The voice agent does not claim the transfer succeeded.


Treat handoff context as a pass/fail test. The receiving agent should get the verification result, the subscription the caller identified, the caller’s request, any offer and response, and the lookup result or error.[SigmaMind AI documents warm transfers and private whispers](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/transfer-call.md) , but those telephony capabilities do not prove that a Gorgias record was created. Ask the receiving agent to confirm what arrived and mark the handoff failed when essential context is missing.


## Pilot scorecard: measurements to define before you launch


Define the pilot scorecard before you review calls. Your brand should set its own pass thresholds and decide how to check each outcome against Recharge, Gorgias, and the receiving phone line.


- **Verified resolution.** For account-specific answers, compare what the voice agent said with the authoritative subscription or charge record. Count a requested account change as complete only after a fresh record check confirms it. Track cancellation requests separately until someone confirms fulfillment.
- **Consent capture rate.** For each approved offer that changes a subscription, check that explicit acceptance was captured before the change. Check that a caller who declines can still proceed with cancellation.
- **Escalation trigger accuracy.** Review whether the agent routes disputes, failed verification, conflicting records, and unavailable data to a person. Record both missed triggers and unnecessary transfers.
- **Transfer and summary delivery success.** Check whether the call reaches the intended person and whether that person receives an accurate account of the caller’s request and actions already taken.
- **Unauthorized disclosure or write incidents.** Count any protected account detail shared before verification or any account change made without the required permission and consent.
- **Unhandled errors.** Count lookup failures, timeouts, and unanswered transfers that leave the caller without a defined next step.


## Conclusion


For a first pilot, let voice AI answer subscription and failed-payment questions only when the caller passes your verification checks and the agent can read current, authoritative records. Let it present a brand-approved retention offer only when the caller qualifies, and require explicit acceptance before any change. Route disputed charges, uncertain records, and unproven write actions to a person. Expand automation only after pilot calls confirm that spoken outcomes match account state and human handoffs work.


## FAQs


**Can voice AI cancel a subscription outright?** Recharge documents a[cancellation action separate from subscription read access](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/2021-11/subscriptions) , but that does not establish a ready-to-use SigmaMind AI phone cancellation workflow. Route cancellation for human execution until your pilot proves caller authorization, permitted write access, consent logging, and confirmation of the final account state.


**What counts as caller verification?** Your brand must define and test an identity check appropriate to the information or action requested. A matching phone number or email address alone should not authorize disclosure or cancellation.


**Can the agent offer a discount when someone asks to cancel?** The agent can present an offer only when your policy confirms eligibility. It should record the caller’s explicit acceptance before any approved plan change and continue with cancellation when the caller declines.


**Who handles payment-card compliance?** Your brand must assess the payment flow and its responsibilities with its payment and compliance advisers. Do not ask callers to speak card numbers into a general recorded or transcribed call. Send payment-method updates through a merchant-approved secure channel.


**What happens when lookup data is stale or unavailable?** The agent should avoid stating a charge or subscription status it cannot confirm. It should transfer the caller to a person and identify the failed lookup without presenting an unverified answer as fact.
